facts.statement: Dracovenator was a medium-sized, ground-dwelling, bipedal carnivore estimated to reach 5.5 to 6.5 meters in length and 250 kilograms in mass.
facts.quote: Dracovenator was a medium-sized, moderately built, ground-dwelling, bipedal carnivore, that could grow up to an estimated 5.5 - 6.5 m in length and 250 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: The genus name Dracovenator is a contraction of the Latin words for "dragon" and "hunter", meaning "dragon hunter".
facts.quote: The genus name is a contraction of the Latin words draco meaning "dragon", and venator meaning "hunter"; thus, "dragon hunter".

facts.statement: Dracovenator was described and named by Adam M. Yates in 2005, with the type species Dracovenator regenti.
facts.quote: Dracovenator was described and named by Adam M. Yates in 2005 and the type species is Dracovenator regenti.

facts.statement: The type material for Dracovenator was discovered at the Upper Drumbo Farm locality in the upper Elliot Formation in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.
facts.quote: The type material BP/1/5243 for Dracovenator was discovered at the "Upper Drumbo Farm" locality in the upper Elliot Formation which is part of the Stormberg Group in Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.

facts.statement: Dracovenator possesses a distinct kink in its upper jaws located between the maxilla and the premaxilla.
facts.quote: Dracovenator has a kink in its upper jaws, between the maxilla and the premaxilla.

facts.statement: Yates assigned Dracovenator to the clade Neotheropoda in 2005.
facts.quote: Yates (2005) assigned Dracovenator to the clade Neotheropoda.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis indicates that Dracovenator forms a clade with the basal theropods Dilophosaurus and Zupaysaurus.
facts.quote: The first cladistic analysis found that this genus formed a clade with the basal theropods Dilophosaurus and Zupaysaurus.

facts.statement: Dracovenator is thought to have preyed on prosauropod dinosaurs within its paleoenvironment.
facts.quote: Dracovenator is thought to have preyed on the prosauropod dinosaurs in its paleoenvironment.

facts.statement: Some estimates suggest Dracovenator was the largest member of the family Dilophosauridae, reaching 7 meters in length.
facts.quote: Otras estimaciones sugieren que Dracovenator era en el más grande de la familia Dilophosauridae con 7 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Dracovenator is unique within its family due to the raised shape of its premaxilla.
facts.quote: Es único en esta familia por la forma de su premaxilar levantado.

facts.statement: Dracovenator regenti was formally described by Yates in 2006.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo, BP/1/5243 de D. regenti, fue formalmente descrito por Yates en el 2006.

facts.statement: The paratype specimen of Dracovenator was discovered by Munyikwa and Raath in 1999.
facts.quote: Munyikwa y Raath descubrieron en 1999 al paratipo BP/1/5278 de Dracovenator

facts.statement: Adam M. Yates named the genus Dracovenator in 2006.
facts.quote: Dracovenator fue descrito y nombrado por Adam M. Yates en 2006

facts.statement: The holotype of Dracovenator was found at the "Granja Drumbo Superior" locality in the Elliot Formation.
facts.quote: El material holotipo de Dracovenator BP/1/5243 fue descubierto en la localidad "Granja Drumbo Superior" en la Formación Elliot

facts.statement: James Kitching and Regent "Lucas" Huma discovered the holotype of Dracovenator.
facts.quote: El holotipo fue descubierto por James Kitching y Regent "Lucas" Huma

facts.statement: The paratype of Dracovenator was discovered in 1981.
facts.quote: El material paratipo BP/1/5278 (que originalmente asignado a Syntarsus rhodesiensis) fue descubierto en 1981

facts.statement: Dracovenator lived from the Hettangian to the Sinemurian, between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Dracovenator are housed at the Bernard Price Institute for Palaeontological Research in Johannesburg, South Africa.
facts.quote: Tanto los especímenes holotipo como paratipo se encuentran en la colección de fósiles del Instituto Paleontológico Bernard Price para la Investigación, que forma parte de la Escuela de Geociencias de la Universidad de Witwatersrand, en Johannesburgo, Sudáfrica.

facts.statement: Yates classified Dracovenator within the family Dilophosauridae alongside the basal theropods Dilophosaurus and Zupaysaurus.
facts.quote: Yates encontró que este género forma parte de la familia Dilophosauridae con los terópodos basales Dilophosaurus y Zupaysaurus.

facts.statement: Dracovenator had a twist in its upper jaw between the maxilla and premaxilla.
facts.quote: Dracovenator tiene una torcedura en su mandíbula superior, entre el maxilar y el premaxilar.

facts.statement: The posterior end of Dracovenator's lower jaw features a variety of masses or protuberances.
facts.quote: El extremo posterior de la mandíbula inferior cuenta con una gran variedad de masas o protuberancias

facts.statement: Researchers believe Dracovenator fed on prosauropods in its paleoenvironment.
facts.quote: Se cree que Dracovenator se habría alimentado de los prosaurópodos de su paleoambiente.

facts.statement: The genus name Dracovenator means "dragon hunter" or "dragon catcher".
facts.quote: El nombre del género Dracovenator significa "cazador de dragones" o "dragón cazador".

facts.statement: The name "Draco" refers to the discovery location in the Drakensberg foothills, meaning "Mountain of the Dragon".
facts.quote: "Draco" se refiere a su descubrimiento en las estribaciones de Drakensberg, que es "Montaña del Dragón".

facts.statement: The species name D. regenti honors the late Regent "Lucas" Huma, who was a field assistant to Professor Kitching.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, D. regenti fue nombrada así en el honor del fallecido Regent "Lucas" Huma, que fue ayudante de campo del profesor Kitching.
